recipes.name: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 large cooked chicken breasts - cut into bite size pieces

steps.text: Bring water, bouillon cubes, and garlic to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in quinoa; reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until quinoa is tender and water has been absorbed, 15 to 20 minutes.
Discard garlic clove and transfer quinoa into a large bowl.
Add chicken, onion, bell pepper, olives, feta cheese, parsley, chives, and salt to quinoa; drizzle lemon juice, balsamic vinegar, and olive oil on top. Stir until evenly mixed.
Serve warm or refrigerate and serve cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
raw_recipe.description: A Mediterranean quinoa salad packed with tender quinoa, feta, red onion, and olives, flavored with lemon and herbs for a light meal full of flavor.

review.reviewBody: Also made a couple of changes, but nothing major. Made it vegetarian, and added some chickpeas to make it more hearty. Also was out of red onion, so used regular onion instead. Excellent flavor, enjoyed this recipe a lot.

This is a good recipe from which one can adapt as needed. I just finished making this and it is indeed tasty. For those who are new to quinoa: you MUST rinse quinoa before cooking it. I am very surprised this recipe didn't include this necessary step. There is a bitter, soapy outer film on quinoa that needs to be rinsed off before cooking. It's very easy - just put the quinoa in a fine-mesh strainer and run cold water over it. I use a small whisk and stir the quinoa around to make sure all of the bitter coating is washed off. I do this for about three minutes. Drain the quinoa and then put it in the pan you're going to cook it in and toast it over medium heat. When the quinoa is dry then add the liquid and bring the mixture to a nice simmer. It helps to cover the quinoa after it's finished cooking to make sure all the liquid is absorbed. So: always, always rinse your quinoa. My tweaks: I added fresh basil in addition to the parsely. I used only 1/2 red onion, and the juice of only 1 lemon. I added oregano, black pepper and a dusting of a nice fruity red pepper. I used a yellow bell pepper instead of a green pepper - orange, yellow and red bell peppers are sweeter and taste better (imho) Plus, they have a better nutritional profile than green peppers. Here is the tweak I added that might raise some eyebrows: as the quinoa was cooling I added about 3/4 cup frozen peas. This cooled the quinoa down so I could add it to the vegetable/chicken mixture without melting the feta. The peas add a nice color and a nice little pop of sweetness to the dish. I omitted the balsamic vinegar and added a cup of sliced cherry tomatoes (Sun golds - quite sweet) When I taste it again tomorrow I may want to add more oregano and pepper. This dish has a very Greek profile, and I think it will benefit from both.

Came out amazing (with some changes)! 

I only used the juice of 1 whole lemon, I would start with half a lemon and go from there.

I marinated 1 lb of chicken breasts in olive oil, lemon juice, red chili flakes, and S&P. Then I cooked the chicken in a large pot, set it aside, and cooked the onion and green pepper in the same pot. Mixed everything else together according to the recipe.

Wow! I have a new favorite. This is so freaking good!! The only thing I did differently was to substitute fresh basil for the parsley and chives. I did use chicken.. I cooked it in a skillet with olive oil and Greek seasoning. Someone suggested chickpeas instead of the chicken. I'm trying that next. I could live on this and nothing else!! Yummy!!

Ok, I did make quite a few changes! 
I used the entire bunch of parsley ( trying to clean out fridge!). I added a cucumber, 2 tomatoes. Omitted the feta and olives. Added dried mint. The large amount of lemon juice I thought would be a waste. I cut it down to less than 1/3 lemon juice. I added 2 tsp rice vinegar instead of balsamic. I am kinda getting tired of balsamic. I also just cooked the quinoa in chicken broth instead of using buillion, and added minced garlic instead of just smashing a clove. I like garlic! Didn't use chives either. It tasted just like tabbouleh!

I've made this a few times for parties. Always a big hit. So easy; so good. Like others, I'm a vegetarian and made some changes - no chicken and use vegetable bouillon. When we have vegan guests, I simply put the feta cheese to the side since I haven't been able to find a vegan version of feta yet. I've also found a few tweaks I like - lighter colored quinoa presents better - looks more appealing. I use a little more lemon juice and whisk that with the balsamic vinegar and olive oil and then drizzle over. I also omit the green peppers because few around me like them. I bet in the cold version, cucumbers are a good addition.

I used the vegetarian better than bouillon, which is now a staple in my pantry. I also carmelized the onion and pepper in a small amount of olive oil prior to adding to the quinoa because I don't like either vegetable raw. It was so delicious! It's definitely become a lunch time staple.

YUM!!!! This salad was delicious. I used red, yellow and orange mini bell peppers because I don't like green and I also seeded and added a tomato (the picture shows something red diced up in it, but nothing red was listed in the ingredients). I also used tomato & basil feta cheese and my leftover Costco rotisserie chicken . It had so much flavor, almost didn't need the dressing. I made it last night and put it in the refrig and we all had it for lunch today. So tasty! My daughter doesn't like bell peppers, so next time I may substitue the bell peppers for a seeded cucumber. Will definitely make again.

This may be a second review, if so, after several years its still a 5-star side/salad for me. This is a great base recipe that can be changed a bit depending on what I have on hand. I always reduce lemon juice to juice of one lemon. Today I omitted chicken, up’d the kalamata olives, added one cup of halved grape tomatoes and about one-third cup grated queso cojita cheese. Delish!
Substituted 15 oz. can of garbanzo beans for the chicken and used 1/2 the amount of olive oil. Wonderful!!! Served over a green salad. Shelton Cabernet Franc pairs well.

We love this salad. We opted not to add chicken and we don’t miss it. I also use only half a red onion, one was way too much in our opinion. We also found that when not using the chicken, only half the vinaigrette is plenty. I whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and balsamic vinegar together before pouring it over the salad. We enjoy it freshly made warm, and have leftovers the next day that are cold.
Was pretty good. Loved the olives and dressing. Would make again. It did get tiresome every day for work for a week though.
Definitely don't add all the lemon juice, oil, and balsamic vinegar at one time! It's very strong. It much better to add to taste (I found about half worked perfectly)

I have been making this for years and love it. I double recipe and only use 3 1/2 C water with chicken bouillon. Tri-colored quinoa, 2 each red, green and yellow bell peppers or more for personal preference and color and just 1 large red onion. Start with 3/4 C lemon juice and 5-6 TBS balsamic vinegar and adjust to your liking. Fantastic!

Very tasty. I served it warm and followed the recipe with the exception of leaving out the onions (due to allergies). It was extremely lemony—almost too much even in in our lemon-loving household—so in future I'm going to drop the lemon juice to 1/2 cup and maybe increase the balsamic vinegar by 1 T. I'm also going to increase the amount of quinoa by 1/2 cup and water by 1 cup, since there was a LOT of the dressing and it could easily have covered half again as much.
I really liked this. I used chick peas instead of chicken and the flavor was perfect with juice from 1.5 lemons. Sodium free bouillion and no added salt.
Great flavor! I slightly reduced the amount of onion (to about 1/2 to 2/3 of the onion) and lemon juice (to about 1/2 cup) and added some more olives (to about 1/2 cup).

Such a tasty and versatile recipe. The textures and flavors are spot on. The refreshing notes from the lemon juice and balsamic vinegar are perfectly balanced by the richness of olive oil and feta cheese. The quinoa adds a subtle yet wonderful texture to the whole salad. And the best part is that you can switch the ingredients as you see fit, you can use a white onion for more sweetness, dill instead of parsley, blue cheese stuffed olives instead of kalamata olives etc. This recipe is a keeper for sure.
Definitely a keeper. I used half the onion and it was perfect.
